top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye for the optical lattice clock. Magic-wavelength trapping removes the lattice light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once. That is a separable invention, distinct from the frequency comb and single-ion clocks. Ye's group carried it to the 1e-18 systematic frontier and many-body-aware operation, and independent Sr and Yb laboratories reproduce it. The two-person allocation is clean and the work is mature. I rank it above no award on its scientific merit, not because the support is unanimous.
recusal_note: No documented connection to Katori or Ye. My listed collaborations are with other atomic and attosecond groups (Lund, ETH Zurich), so no recusal-level conflict is apparent from the profile, though precision atomic theory is close to my field.
